# **Ilana Interview Guide**

WordPets — teacher input before building activities & daily practice · 30–45 min · recorded  
*"I've been building a practice app called WordPets that would work alongside your teaching — your students do short daily practice between your sessions, earn rewards for a virtual pet, and you see who's practicing in a dashboard. Before I build the actual lesson content and activities, I want to make sure I'm building what you actually need. These questions are to help me understand your teaching, not to test you — there are no right answers. Feel free to say 'I don't know' or 'this question doesn't make sense.'"*

## **Part 1 · Your Teaching** (5–10 min)

*These questions ground everything. Don't rush them.*

1. **Walk me through a typical lesson with a 7-year-old student.** What do you do at the start? Middle? End? What activities work best with them?  
   Here is an outline of what i had sent to chat gpt before about a model lesson for a 5-6 year old, pre-k level

Letter book- C  
 Intro video- ABC SEE HEAR DO theme TPR plus song cc  
 Image with the letter, some kinda tracing  
 Letter formation- high middle downstairs (house)  
 Phonemic awareness- sound and circle (boy crying, boy happy)  
 Identification- circle all the “c” words in a group of many (cups in a closet)  
 Identification- circle the c words in a block or rows (pencil, camera, car, candle, yarn, cat, book)  
 Writing practice- upper \- and lowercase- print a page- spelling- find the c on keyboard/typing skills  
 Concept- sounds- similar/dif/ other skills  
 Drawing/game/craft- pet time- reward (link to hands-on craft)  
 Story-audio- comprehension  
 Songs- something about a snake scares sam silly  
 Reward for finishing that level

Unlock pet- what can they do with them- feed, walk, train

Craft extension video telling them what materials they need and explanation  
 Coloring page  
 Game- guess the animal- I live in the desert, I have 1 or 2 humps and drink lots of water I am a…click to reveal (audio)  
 Paper craft- food- show a video of what foods start with c and encourage kids to get it

Not sure if you are asking for a private or group lesson? I will give you an example from a third grade class and up too, since most of my classes are third-eighth grade. I can also give examples of first grade classes I have taught in the past. 

I will usually start with a fun warm-up consisting of a riddle, a rebus puzzle, or a fun short writing prompt. If it’s a lower grade it can be a question like “Do you prefer lemonade or ice-coffee? (optional extension) Why? A sample answer, depending on their level can even just be the one word answer and a drawing of it. I then differentiate and use this method across most grades. If it’s an older group then I would ask them to defend their answer, give me pros and cons of each, have a classroom debate about what is better. Other fun warm-ups include knock knock jokes, more bizarre writing prompts like would you rather questions like would you rather have one eye or 3 ears- the more unusual the better. For older kids we can talk about more controversial topics, philosophy, or current events- recently we have talked about the pros and cons of self-driving cars, ai-tutors vs real teachers, and if you can separate the art from the artist despite his/her controversial or problematic views (should we enjoy the literature of Roald Dahl despite him being a raving anti-semite and we are Jewish). The older kids grades 5th and up really enjoy this discussion then we turn it into a written response. Another fun opener/hook is a cute comic book strip- snoopy, or any other 4 part strip that has a funny message often connected to school. Here is an example:

![][image1]

The point is to engage the kids at the very start of the lesson.

Next, we will do a few pages from the spelling and reading workbook for younger kids, for older kids we do novel studies and read a chapter, discuss new vocab, themes from the book. For an even younger child, I will try to cover written production and reception (writing, dictation, recognition of a new letter or words- identifying it in a group of letter etc). We will do phonemic awareness circle in a row the pictures that start with the target letter. Then we will read a short story or fable or I will read it to them that’s somehow connected to the letter- if we do B for bear so maybe I will read them a goldilocks story. If I have the tablet with a one on one so they can click on the target letter to distinguish it from others, or if it’s a group so I can write on the board. Then we will read short CVC words to tie in review of previously learnt sounds. I try to tie in a creative activity too, maybe a craft. At the end of the lesson I will review with them what we covered, sort of as an exit-ticket.

2. **What do you currently assign between sessions?** Worksheets? Reading? Writing? How do you send it — WhatsApp, email, handouts?   
   Almost nothing- I update parents with a short summary of what we covered and maybe some pics from class or a review sheet for a quiz- I don’t burden kids or parents with homework, but I do want parents to be updated with what we are doing.   
3. **Of the students you assign homework to, roughly what percentage actually do it?** Your best guess.  
   I don’t think homework should be a part of the app- it’s all done at home. I am not a big fan of homework at all because most students don’t do it, and it puts pressure on the parents.   
4. **What's the \#1 thing holding your students back right now?** Don't say "reading" — get specific. Confidence? Decoding? Memory? Attention? Parent support?  
   Motivation  
5. **Which of your current students are you most frustrated with?** What's the pattern you see?  
   Ones that have little desire to learn and/or cause disciplinary problems in class. During a one on one online app I think disciplinary issues are minimised or non-existent.   
6. **Which students are you most excited about?** What makes them work?  
   The ones who genuinely seem interested in the content

## **Part 2 · Content** (5–10 min)

7. **Do you create teaching materials yourself, reuse from other sources, or both?** How do you decide?  
   I use a combination of my own materials and I source from reading eggs, abc see hear do, Beginning letterbooks, online resources, gratitude journals for writing prompts, lists of would you rather prompts etc. I pick what is both engaging and actually educational. I also use super-teacher worksheets sometimes which is a great site.   
     
8. **If you have a pile of PDFs/worksheets/passages you already use, would you want to upload those into an app, or would it feel like extra work?**  
   Well I am concerned about copyright issues for that- I would rather create new content with the assistance of AI for the app- but if you want to model it from existing material then I would definitely upload it.   
9. **For reading passages — do you pick from books, websites, write your own, or something else?** What level of English is appropriate for your 6–8 year olds?  
   I love red cat reading for this age and mostly use their books, I also bring in Dr. Seuss or PD Eastman, I don’t usually have time to write my own stories.   
10. **Do you use sight word lists (Dolch/Fry) or something else for vocabulary?**  
    Yes absolutely for sight words I refer to dolch/fry list.   
11. **What kind of spelling practice actually works with your kids?**  
    Quizzes, games

## **Part 3 · The App Idea** (10–15 min)

*This is the core. Slow down here.*

12. **What's your honest reaction to the idea of a companion app?** Excited, skeptical, curious, overwhelmed?  
    Totally excited but also overwhelmed  
13. **If this app existed tomorrow, would you actually use it with your students, or does it feel like one more thing on your plate?**  
    I would use it with my private students immediately.   
14. **What would make a 7-year-old actually open the app every day?** In your experience, what hooks these kids?  
    The pet idea, colorful, fun content  
15. **What would make YOU use it with students vs forget it exists?**  
    I won’t need to be reminded, but I want to use it for future students, not just current. I want it to primarily be to get new students- and to remove the need for me to teach them live.   
16. **Is there something you wish existed for your teaching that doesn't?** (Don't constrain to apps — could be anything.)  
    A personal assistant to act as a liaison between me and parents  
17. **What would you NOT want the app to do?** Things that would annoy you, embarrass your students, or create more work.  
    Be too bloated and confusing for parents and kids.   
18. **The pet thing — is that appealing to your age group?** Would kids name a pet, care about it, come back for it? Or is that more of a younger-kid thing?  
    I think it’s cool for almost everyone (even I would want one)

## **Part 4 · Logistics** (5–10 min)

19. **How many of your current students would you pilot this with? Which ones and why?** Don't feel obligated — if the answer is zero, that's useful to know.  
    Around 5 students but they are not all beginners, they are various levels, some emerging readers (fourth grade students who are behind). If I launch it to my students from the school, so then I could get another 5-10 on board I think  
    Forgot to add- we can use beta/pilot on all of our 4 kids  
20. **How much time are you realistically willing to spend on this per week?** Be honest — 5 min? 30 min? An hour? More?  
    I think 30 min to an hour, wish I could give more  
21. **What about the parents?** Will they install an app for their kid without convincing, or not?  
    I have excellent rapport with parents they are mostly my friends and probably will be willing to do it  
22. **Do you charge parents separately for between-session work right now, or is it included in your teaching fee?**  
    No I don’t charge anything extra  
23. **What's your biggest hesitation about this whole project?** What could go wrong?  
    My biggest hesitation is it won’t make money and we will continue to be in dire straights, and that it will take up my time when I could be teaching privately instead and it would result in an income loss. 

## **Part 5 · Speech Recognition Test** (5 min — optional but valuable)

*If Eli can play a sample of Whisper transcribing a 7-year-old reading aloud:*

24. **Listen to this — a kid reading a passage, and here's what the AI transcribed.** Would you trust this to tell a kid "correct" or "try again"?  
    I dont see the passage  
25. **If the AI transcription is imperfect, would you rather have:**  
    (a) AI grades strictly — kid sees pass/fail  
    (b) AI grades leniently — always says "great job"  
    (c) AI just records the attempt and you review it when you have time  
    C- for now til I can trust it or it proves it’s measuring accuratley

## **Part 6 · Ilana's Questions** (5–10 min)

26. **What questions do YOU have for me about this project?**  
    Should I realistically work less so I can focus on this until it is successful?   
27. **What should I be asking that I'm not asking?**  
    I want to focus on higher levels too, not just pre K and K and first grade, could we come up with a template that works as differentiation for several grades with extension opportunities?  
28. **Is there anyone else we should talk to before building this?** Other teachers, parents, kids?  
    Eliaou needs to give his input too maybe you should interview him.
